parameters.formDescription: One sample, one form. You get a QR at the end: print it, or photograph the screen. Whoever receives the sample scans it to log the arrival.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: Everything an operator changes lives here. Spreadsheet id and chat id are the two that must.

nodes.name: Normalise dispatch form
nodes.notes: Form labels in, column names out. The only place the two vocabularies meet.

nodes.name: Generate ID
nodes.notes: The clock and the random source are read here and passed in, so the library stays testable.

nodes.name: Look up spec
nodes.notes: Zero rows halts the dispatch. Nothing is ever judged against a default spec.

nodes.name: Build register row
nodes.notes: Every column the schema names, blanks included, so the sheet never shifts a column.

nodes.name: Register the sample
nodes.notes: Row one of the lifecycle, straight from the Code node before it.

parameters.content:
## Sample Trail

A sample goes out, arrives, gets assessed, and someone approves or rejects it against contract spec. Five flows, one workflow, all of it from a phone.

**What you need**
- A store: n8n Data Tables as shipped, or a spreadsheet if you switch the store nodes
- A chat bot token and the chat id you want messages in
- A model credential, for reading a photographed grading sheet or a typed reading
- A mail credential, only if you want the QR emailed as well

**Before you run it**
1. Open the Settings node in each flow. The store ids and the chat id are the two things that must change.
2. Put your quality parameters in the spec store, one row per parameter.
3. Set SLA_DAYS to how long a grader has.

The arrival form prefills the sample id from the QR **only on the production URL**. On a test URL the field renders empty and looks broken. That is n8n, not this workflow.

## Flow A: Dispatch

A form on a phone, an id, and a QR that opens the arrival form. No scanner, no app, no hardware.

A contract with no spec rows halts here and says so. Nothing is judged against a default spec.
